current_companion_addendum.qualified_final_current_selector: Flat canonical final findings.json explicitly required by bound configuration and present in qualified frozen final inventory; draft versions excluded from phase1. No versioned Vnnn stream configured or inferred.
current_companion_addendum.all_current_assertions_obligation: Assess every current finding body and material assertion in this companion together with the bound standalone report and assigned eligibility; no sampling.

coverage_meaning: Every material assertion across the complete supplied standalone report and all fourteen full current finding bodies, plus all six assigned facets, was reviewed; no sampling.

claims.claim: Prepared/final status; full input/source reads, TASK lengths, no fetching, finding/acquisition records and operation compliance.
claims.reason: Final files are frozen as supplied. Original TASK, native operations and acquisition records are not admitted; their sizes, reads, independence and provenance cannot be established in phase 1.

claims.claim: Fixed source title/date/editor/copyright institution, URL alias, original/view hash, 36,980 bytes, 896 lines and source-section register.
claims.reason: Source and catalog pins match exactly. OME/U. Dundee is the copyright attribution; the editor affiliation is German BioImaging e.V. Header URLs all point to /0.5 in this capture.

claims.claim: Five-slice 21-line plan and five-line brief are supplied.
claims.reason: The sliced plan is separately pinned; its substantive content matches the thin read-only local viewer scope.

claims.claim: External Zarr/OME-XML/UDUNITS/OMERO documents are references rather than admitted evidence; local-only transfer and live implementation limits.
claims.reason: The report scopes transfer correctly; no external document or native tool behavior is verified here.

claims.claim: Zarr v3 and broadly permitted features unless explicitly disallowed; chunk metadata and local/HTTP/object storage.
claims.reason: The crucial exception is retained. All features are not universally unrestricted because labels and image axes have specific constraints.

claims.claim: A reader feature subset may fail to decode valid data; reader breadth is a product decision and partial chunk loading an engineering approach.
claims.reason: A reasonable capability/engineering inference, not observed performance. Real emitted codecs and addressing details remain unverified.

claims.claim: Image groups, optional omero, separate arrays, arbitrary axis/level names, declared ordering and up to five axes with time/channel/space order.
claims.reason: The full body explicitly preserves omero optionality and validation before relying on axis order.

claims.claim: Label dimensions must equal image dimensions or be one if irrelevant.
claims.reason: The cited layout example says should. The full finding promotes it to MUST and cannot establish a universal dimension-admission constraint.

claims.claim: Discover levels through declared paths/order; labels container is the route; unrelated-group behavior is defined only for collections.
claims.reason: Metadata is authoritative; no source ban on all supplemental scanning follows from this choice.

claims.claim: HCS plate/row/well hierarchy and mandatory specifications, with empty rows/wells discouraged.
claims.reason: Required hierarchy and empty-group conditions are correctly separated.

claims.claim: Sparse plates and metadata-driven well/field traversal reuse image pipelines.
claims.reason: A valid source-to-plan implication. Exclusive refusal of scanning is a proposed discovery policy, not an explicit source prohibition.

claims.claim: Whether well field paths may traverse intermediate groups is unspecified.
claims.reason: The literal mandatory alphanumeric-only path rule rules out slash-separated traversal. Behavior for an invalid or missing path remains unspecified, but path syntax is not wholly open.

claims.claim: attributes.ome, string hierarchy-consistent version, gate 0.5 behavior and explanatory handling of mixed versions.
claims.reason: The version/namespace distinction and explicit admission signal are clear. Reject versus disclosed best effort is expressly a product choice.

claims.claim: Required unique names, rank and per-level dimension_names; recommended type/unit with custom values.
claims.reason: Axis-to-array identity is correctly grounded, without forcing standard names or guaranteed unit presence.

claims.claim: Calibrated coordinates are possible only when units exist; absent units may fall back to raw indices labeled uncalibrated.
claims.reason: Unknown units prevent a named physical-unit claim, but known transforms still define a coordinate mapping and relative factors. A raw-index fallback must not silently discard supplied scale/offset metadata.

claims.claim: Custom/missing type handling, formatting and unit conversion are product choices with external grammar unresolved.
claims.reason: A graceful unsupported-role policy is permissible; axes still need to satisfy the multiscales spatial constraints.

claims.claim: Transitional collections, layout 3, plate precedence/exclusivity, OME-XML sidecar and MetadataOnly content.
claims.reason: The full body retains the existence and content distinction, although its governing-summary phrase OME-XML details SHOULD needs care: if XML is supplied, content constraints are MUST.

claims.claim: Series is optional, string paths ordered to XML if supplied; numeric groups only without series and plate; reader SHOULD/MAY policies.
claims.reason: The full finding preserves both discovery conditions and does not require a particular collection UI.

claims.claim: Summary series order always matches XML Images and consecutive-numbered fallback is unconditional.
claims.reason: The summary omits if XML is provided and neither series nor plate; the full body restores them. Both remain current, so the summary cannot be treated as a complete unconditional rule.

claims.claim: The bioformats2raw layout is real tool output information and source-grounded interop target; later replacement and external XML rules unresolved.
claims.reason: This credits the source tool/layout information without claiming current implementation tolerance or a tested native interop result.

claims.claim: General transform types, identity default, inline/binary vectors and sequential list order.
claims.reason: The vocabulary and vector alternatives are explicit.

claims.claim: Apply ordered transforms and support path vectors or explicitly refuse them; binary encoding/dtype/byte order is not specified here.
claims.reason: A sound correctness/capability proposal. The actual binary read mechanics are an unresolved dependency.

claims.claim: Multiscales rank/type/order, group-relative declared levels, dimensional consistency and one required scale.
claims.reason: These apply within each multiscales dictionary and do not require fixed folder names or reduction ratios.

claims.claim: Physical scale is normal; relative factor is fallback when scaling is unavailable; translation follows scale, matching vectors; group transforms follow dataset transforms.
claims.reason: The full finding preserves the principal fallback condition and transform composition order.

claims.claim: The required scale defaults to 1.0 and physical calibration is always derivable because scale is mandatory.
claims.reason: Default 1.0 is conditional on unavailable/inapplicable scaling and no downsampling. Such values do not establish physical calibration. A mandatory vector permits a mapping, not universally known physical units.

claims.claim: zyx is a general spatial-order SHOULD.
claims.reason: The source condition includes yx as the image plane and the other anisotropic stack axis z. This is broader than a rule for all three-space axes.

claims.claim: Recommended descriptive keys; multiple named entries require chooser or documented fallback.
claims.reason: The keys are SHOULD. Name/first-fallback and chunk-size choice are informative example guidance; they do not impose a universal reader UI requirement.

claims.claim: Optional transitional omero, conditional channels/RGB/window fields, example rdefs and external display semantics.
claims.reason: The body accurately distinguishes example conventions and normative field rules, and proposes explicit absent-metadata fallbacks.

claims.claim: Channel-count mismatch with the array is a malformed case.
claims.reason: Count matching is an informative example comment, not an explicit mandatory cardinality rule in the supplied normative sentences. It can be an unsupported display case or validation warning without inventing a format MUST.

claims.claim: Integer label whitelist, arbitrary names and intermediate groups without metadata, required paths with completeness SHOULD.
claims.reason: Names and hierarchy rules support discovery, and the report correctly retains the all-labels SHOULD.

claims.claim: Label multiscales and mandatory equal level count.
claims.reason: Count parity is a format rule; it is not registration proof.

claims.claim: Equal counts guarantee level-for-level alignment and source-equal-or-singleton dimensions are mandatory.
claims.reason: The source says same dimensions/transforms are usual. Count parity alone gives neither equal grids nor origin alignment; the dimension comment is should-level illustrative text.

claims.claim: image-label SHOULD; colors/version have conditional types; keyed integer IDs, optional RGBA/alpha, recommended reader palette use, extra keys.
claims.reason: Value-type MUSTs are conditional on the recommended keys being supplied. No explicit child-key-presence MUST is credited.

claims.claim: Optional properties and source, keyed arbitrary nonuniform metadata, relative image path/default, approximate half-opacity worked example.
claims.reason: The metadata facts and worked example are accurate. Actual relative-source resolution and exact categorical decoding are not specified.

claims.claim: Missing colors/rendering blend details and singleton-label display are product decisions; supplemental scanning is allowed choice.
claims.reason: The source does not supply a complete default palette or blending implementation. Scanning is not forbidden.

claims.claim: Plate required rows/columns/version/wells, all physical rows/columns, exact names and indexes; acquisition fields and conditional types.
claims.reason: Detailed mandatory/recommended/optional field constraints are supplied in the companion body.

claims.claim: Dense/sparse examples; grid, field choice and acquisition filtering may follow metadata, with missing-path behavior and field ordering unresolved.
claims.reason: Useful product alternatives; a particular grid UI is not itself a source requirement.

claims.claim: Required fields list, unique alphanumeric case-sensitive paths, conditional acquisition reference, recommended string well version and examples.
claims.reason: Acquisition conditionality and well-version strength are accurately preserved.

claims.claim: Never directory-scan fields; acquisition filtering is optional and missing required reference is invalid.
claims.reason: The normative list supplies authoritative identity and mandatory references. Never scanning is a proposed discovery policy rather than a format prohibition; supplemental scans cannot override metadata.

claims.claim: Field paths through intermediate groups are an unresolved format permission.
claims.reason: Alphanumeric-only required path syntax already constrains separators. Missing-path runtime handling remains open, but the stated syntactic uncertainty is too broad.

claims.claim: Transitional reader MUST/SHOULD expectations vary by metadata, writing usually MAY; comments forbidden and camelCase has legacy exceptions.
claims.reason: The generic policy is conditional, rather than requiring every transitional feature unconditionally.

claims.claim: All interoperability requires transitional reading; spec imposes reading duties only.
claims.reason: Declared supported interop profiles may require relevant transitional features. Generic policy also discusses writing, and key-level reader expectations are not universally mandatory. Read-only viewing triggers no write obligation.

claims.claim: Exact key strings should be used, not uniform case conversion; maximumfieldcount is a legacy snake_case example and naming may be a capture artifact.
claims.reason: Exact spellings are supported. maximumfieldcount is all lowercase, not snake_case; the source expressly acknowledges legacy naming differences. Their ultimate acquisition provenance remains unknown.

claims.claim: Pinned edition/header URLs/status, draft uncertainty, migrations, history dates and implementation pointer.
claims.reason: These are capture statements, not live currency checks or proof of native reader behavior.

claims.claim: RFC keyword/lowercase rules and normative-text exceptions distinguish recommendations, options and obligations.
claims.reason: The full body correctly preserves exceptions for examples, notes and explicit non-normative sections.

claims.claim: All non-example text is normative.
claims.reason: Notes and explicitly non-normative sections are additional exceptions; the full body supplies the correct rule, but the summary wording is incomplete.

claims.claim: 0.4-era filesets are v2 and accepting them would require Zarr v2 support.
claims.reason: The history establishes adoption of v3 in 0.5, but does not explicitly establish v2 storage for every 0.4 fileset. This is an unverified compatibility assertion, not admitted source evidence.

claims.claim: Every non-example/notes prose statement carries RFC 2119 force.
claims.reason: Text can be normative as a descriptive conformance assertion without every sentence becoming a MUST. Strength must still follow the actual clause and applicable keyword.

claims.claim: Obligation, optional capability and product-decision table gives all listed normative field/rank/order/type checks and reader alternatives.
claims.reason: The listed mandatory surfaces are mostly correct. Collection conditions, informative multiple-entry guidance and assumed v2 history require the separate qualifications above; source silent/error policy is product choice.

claims.claim: Keep the fixture disclaimer; add metadata-driven plain/collection/HCS image discovery and surface multiple images.
claims.reason: A sound broad-plan improvement, conditional on declared capabilities and with source reader SHOULD strength.

claims.claim: Use declared level list rather than names and a name/first-fallback entry choice.
claims.reason: Level authority is normative; the multiple-entry UI pattern is informative product guidance.

claims.claim: Axes-driven controls with custom types/absent units and optional omero defaults plus fallbacks.
claims.reason: A source-compatible product proposal. Explicit absent-versus-singleton control policy is still missing.

claims.claim: Dataset-then-group composition, inline/path capability and mandatory scale with default 1 permit correct coordinates.
claims.reason: Order and capability disclosure are correct. Mandatory scale does not guarantee physical calibration, and fallback 1.0 is conditional; a numeric offset check is absent.

claims.claim: Count parity enables aligned overlays with colors/alpha and unlisted-label risk.
claims.reason: It enables a candidate correspondence, not verified registration. Actual identity and transforms must be resolved first.

claims.claim: Background/cancellation are format-neutral, partial reads are an engineering basis, specific syntax/version/axis/type/path failures can be reported.
claims.reason: Concrete invalid-input facts are supported. Feedback/cancellation/performance remain product behavior, not native guarantees.

claims.claim: Interop and version envelope are open; read-only scope is compatible; acceptance should include proposed fixtures.
claims.reason: Read-only compatibility and explicit future testing are sound. Relevant transitional support varies by profile; unverified v2 history and universal reading-only claims require qualifications.

claims.claim: Both groups and every brief requirement are mapped; aggregate scope equals the full brief.
claims.reason: The topical map is visible and both groups are addressed. It is not complete satisfaction of six facets; registration, categorical precision and calibration checks remain missing.

claims.claim: All source sections/eight keys and every MUST/SHOULD/MAY cluster were mapped and re-scanned.
claims.reason: All eight keys have current finding bodies; actual re-scan operations are unverified. A topical map does not prove no omitted conditions or every clause received a correct disposition.

claims.claim: Example listing says all labels while normative completeness SHOULD controls.
claims.reason: This accurately rejects strengthening the example listing into a universal MUST.

claims.claim: Example-only rdefs is not a MUST; exact maximumfieldcount spelling retained.
claims.reason: These are useful exact-condition checks.

claims.claim: All five plan slices and brief clauses were mapped, none unmapped.
claims.reason: This is true as a visible topical map; it does not assert a tested implementation or complete answer to every eligible facet.

claims.claim: Fixed source scope cannot verify live implementation behavior or post-capture changes; Tools/migration references are not supplied.
claims.reason: The principal runtime interop limitation is honest. Named tool/layout information elsewhere is still credited rather than erased.

claims.claim: Detailed binary transforms, units conversion, OME-XML and OMERO semantics need future sources.
claims.reason: These specific external or underspecified implementation dependencies are supported as limits.

claims.claim: Missing well.version and display ordering have no prescribed runtime response.
claims.reason: Missing recommended version is not itself a mandatory type violation; runtime/display policy is not stated.

claims.claim: Error behavior for invalid versions/counts/missing paths or duplicate entry names is product work; later errata unvisited.
claims.reason: These specific runtime policies and post-capture limits are not resolved by the supplied source.

claims.reason: Declared resolution order does not mandate every physical or array-axis extent decrease, and count equality does not guarantee pixel-grid registration. Such properties need defined synthetic fixture geometry or explicit product capability constraints.

Intermediate paths/default and count are described. Actual relative-source association, coordinate relationship and explicit refusal of unsupported geometry are not resolved; count-based alignment is overclaimed.
